Report Description
***WEB REPORT*** ON 07/17/13 AT 0658 HOURS, SE TRAIN DISPATCHER ADVISED TRAIN U14714 WITH LOCOMOTIVES CSXT 5497, 446, AND 254 (ALL DVR) DERAILED THREE LOADED COAL CARS AT MP 000 350.2 ON THE S AND N A NORTH SUBDIVISION. THIS WAS LOCATED IN A RURAL AREA SOUTH OF HANCEVILLE. AL. TWO CARS ARE REPORTED ON THEIR SIDES AND ONE LEANING. HANCEVILLE POLICE AND CULLMAN COUNTY WERE NOTIFIED. CRISIS COMMUNICATIONS MANAGER, WAS NOTIFIED AND ADVISED SWS ENVIRONMENTAL CONTRACTORS ARE RESPONDING FROM BIRMINGHAM, AL. NO INJURIES WERE REPORTED. AT 0747 HOURS, CULLMAN POLICE ADVISED THEY HAVE CLEARED THE SCENE AND REPORT NO WATERWAYS ARE AFFECTED. AT 0932 HOURS, NASHVILLE CHIEF TRAIN DISPATCHER ADVISED THE MAIN LINE TRACK WAS NOT AFFECTED, DERAILMENT WAS ON THE SIDING TRACK. ON 7/19/13 AT 0532 HOURS, IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE TOTAL COST WAS $150,000.00, NRC IS SUBMITTED DUE TO TOTAL COST. AT 1005 HOURS, ROADMASTER, REQUESTED LOCAL GAS AND SEWER DEPARTMENT RESPOND FOR LOCATES. CULLMAN COUNTY WAS NOTIFIED AND RESPONDING.

***WEB REPORT*** ON 07/17/13 AT 0658 HOURS, SE TRAIN DISPATCHER ADVISED TRAIN U14714 WITH LOCOMOTIVES CSXT 5497, 446, AND 254 (ALL DVR) DERAILED THREE LOADED COAL CARS AT MP 000 350.2 ON THE S AND N A NORTH SUBDIVISION. THIS WAS LOCATED IN A RURAL AREA SOUTH OF HANCEVILLE. AL. TWO CARS ARE REPORTED ON THEIR SIDES AND ONE LEANING. HANCEVILLE POLICE AND CULLMAN COUNTY WERE NOTIFIED. CRISIS COMMUNICATIONS MANAGER, WAS NOTIFIED AND ADVISED SWS ENVIRONMENTAL CONTRACTORS ARE RESPONDING FROM BIRMINGHAM, AL. NO INJURIES WERE REPORTED. AT 0747 HOURS, CULLMAN POLICE ADVISED THEY HAVE CLEARED THE SCENE AND REPORT NO WATERWAYS ARE AFFECTED. AT 0932 HOURS, NASHVILLE CHIEF TRAIN DISPATCHER ADVISED THE MAIN LINE TRACK WAS NOT AFFECTED, DERAILMENT WAS ON THE SIDING TRACK. ON 7/19/13 AT 0532 HOURS, IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE TOTAL COST WAS $150,000.00, NRC IS SUBMITTED DUE TO TOTAL COST. AT 1005 HOURS, ROADMASTER, REQUESTED LOCAL GAS AND SEWER DEPARTMENT RESPOND FOR LOCATES. CULLMAN COUNTY WAS NOTIFIED AND RESPONDING.

THE ANOMALY EXHIBITED DARK EDGES WITH SHARP CONTRAST TO ITS SURROUNDINGS AND A LONG STRIPE OF SILVERY SHEEN THROUGHOUT MUCH OF THE ANOMALY INDICATING THICKER OIL. THE ANOMALY CONTINUED INTO THE NEXT SWATH, BUT WAS ABRUPTLY CUT OFF BY A LARGE CLOUD, SIMILAR TO THE TOP HALF OF THE ANOMALY CAPTURED HERE. UNCERTAINTIES: NO IMMEDIATE POINT SOURCE COULD BE DETECTED AS THERE ARE NUMEROUS FACILITIES IN THE AREA AND A VESSEL OF SOME SORT IS LOCATED NEAR THE CLOUD COVER AND ANOMALY. ADDITIONALLY, CLOUDS COVER BOTH ENDS OF THE ANOMALY, SO THE SOURCE AND FULL EXTENT CANNOT BE DETERMINED. MAPS AND SHAPEFILES CAN BE ACCESSED AT: WWW.OSPO.NOAA.GOV/PRODUCTS/OCEAN/MARINEPOLLUTION/

properties.content:

Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: NOAA SHIP OKEANOS EXPLORER
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 41.614347, -71.409235 (Approximated from street_address)
Reported Sheen Size: 5 feet by 40 feet (area 200 sq. ft.)
SkyTruth Minimum Estimate: 0 gallons
Report Description
[WEB REPORT] WHILE CONDUCTING A WEIGHT TEST OF THE SHIP'S PORT SIDE SMALL BOAT DAVIT, A THE CHECK VALVE ON THE HYDRAULIC FLUID RESERVOIR FOR THE WINCH FAILED, CAUSING HYDRAULIC FLUID TO SPILL ONTO THE DECK AND INTO THE WATER. APPROXIMATELY ONE QUART TOTAL WAS LOST, BOTH IN THE WATER ON DECK, APPROXIMATELY 8 OUNCES OF FLUID REACHED THE WATER. THE SHEEN OBSERVED IN THE WATER WAS APPROXIMATELY 40 FEET WIDE AND 5 FEET IN LENGTH. ABSORBENT DIAPERS WERE DEPLOYED ON THE DECK AND THE FREEING PORT WAS BLOCKED USING ABSORBENT MATERIAL. THE SHEEN DISSIPATED QUICKLY, WITHIN A FEW MINUTES. NO ABSORBENTS WERE DEPLOYED IN THE WATER. THE SHIP IS MOORED STARBOARD SIDE TO THE PIER.

properties.summary: Incident Type: FIXED - NRC Report ID: 1009196 - Medium Affected: SOIL - Suspected Responsible Party: US EPA
properties.content:
Report Details
NRC Report ID: 1009196
Incident Time: 2012-04-17 16:00:00
Nearest City: Winnfield, LA
Location: AMERICAN CREOSOTE SUPERFUND SITE LAD000239814 1109 FRONT STREET
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: CREOSOTE
Medium Affected: SOIL
Suspected Responsible Party: US EPA
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 31.917692, -92.636385 (Approximated from street_address)
Reported Spill Volume: 0.5 gallons
Report Description
ON TUESDAY APRIL 17, 2012 DURING O&M AT THE AMERICAN CREOSOTE WORKS SUPERFUND SITE, THE FIELD ENGINEER, IDENTIFIED A SMALL CREOSOTE SPILL ON THE GROUND NEAR TWO FRAC TANKS THAT ARE USED FOR STORAGE OF GROUNDWATER/CREOSOTE MIXTURE. AS PART OF ONGOING TREATABILITY STUDY OPERATIONS, EXTRACTED GROUNDWATER STORED IN FRAC TANKS IS TRANSFERRED TO THE ONSITE PROCESS LIQUID TREATMENT SYSTEM (PLTS). THE EXTRACTED GROUNDWATER/CREOSOTE WAS CONVEYED TO THE PLTS USING A 2 INCH POLYESTER DISCHARGE HOSE. THE HOSE HAD A PUNCTURE, ABOUT THE SIZE OF A PENNY AND A GROUNDWATER/CREOSOTE MIXTURE TRANSFERRED FOR A PERIOD OF 20 MINUTES. THE IMPACTED SOIL WAS EXCAVATED AND PLACED INSIDE A 55 GALLON DRUM. A VISUAL INSPECTION OF THE SPILL AREA WAS MADE TO DETERMINE THAT ALL IMPACTED SOIL WAS REMOVED. THE GROUNDWATER/CREOSOTE MIXTURE RELEASED TO THE GROUND HAS BEEN ESTIMATED AT 2 GALLONS WITH HALF A GALLON OF THAT AMOUNT BEING FREE PHASE CREOSOTE. THE AMOUNT OF SOIL EXCAVATED FROM THE IMPACTED AREA HAS BEEN ESTIMATED BETWEEN 400 - 450 LB. THIS SITE IS A FORMER WOOD TREATING SITE UNDERGOING LONG-TERM REMEDIAL ACTION. THE SPILL AREA CONTAINS A ONE TO TWO FOOT CLEAN SOIL COVER WHICH IS UNDERLAIN BY EXISTING CONTAMINATED SOILS. CH2M HILL WILL MAKE MODIFICATIONS TO THE LIQUID TRANSFER PROCESS TO PREVENT RELEASES OF GROUNDWATER/CREOSOTE MIXTURE INTO THE GROUND. A HIGH-DENSITY POLYETHYLENE (HDPE) PIPE CONFIGURATION WILL REPLACE THE CURRENT 2” POLYESTER DISCHARGE HOSE USED FOR THE TRANSFER OF GROUNDWATER TO THE PLTS. IN ADDITION, A LEAK TEST WILL BE PERFORMED USING CLEAN WATER PRIOR TO PLACING THE CONVEYANCE PIPE IN OPERATION. INSPECTION OF THE HDPE CONVEYANCE PIPE WILL BE SCHEDULED PERIODICALLY TO ASSESS THE INTEGRITY OF THE PIPE.

Nearest City: Dauphin Island, AL
Incident Type: MOBILE
Material: HYDRAULIC OIL
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: ALABAMA DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION
Skytruth Analysis
CALLER STATED THERE WAS A SPILL OF MATERIALS FROM A STATE VEHICLE REPLACING A STOP SIGN. THE VEHICLE WAS A TRACTOR LIKE TRUCK AND THE MATERIALS WERE SPILLED ONTO THE ROADWAY AND ONTO A PRIVATE DRIVEWAY. CALLER STATED THE TRUCK BLEW A HYDRAULIC LINE WHICH RESULTED IN A SPILL OF MATERIALS INTO THE STORM DRAIN. CALLER STATED THE EMPLOYEES REPAIRED THE TRUCK IN THE DRIVEWAY OF A PRIVATE RESIDENT WHICH RESULTED IN ADDITIONAL MATERIALS SPILLING. CALLER STATED THIS IS NOT THE FIRST TIME THERE WAS A SPILL ON THE ROADWAY, ABOUT ONE MONTH AGO THERE WAS A SPILL OF HYDRAULIC OIL WHEN THE WORKERS WERE PAINTING LINES ON THE ROADWAY.

properties.title: NRC Report: Oil, Misc: Lubricating in Cheo near Robbinsville, NC
properties.summary: Incident Type: FIXED - NRC Report ID: 1023369 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: ALCOA
properties.content:
Report Details
NRC Report ID: 1023369
Incident Time: 2012-09-04 12:15:00
Nearest City: Robbinsville, NC
Location: SANTEETLAH HYDROELECTRIC FACILITY NCSR 1247 RYMERS FERRY TAPOCO
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: OIL, MISC: LUBRICATING
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: ALCOA
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 35.356690, -83.806659 (Approximated from ZIP)
Reported Spill Volume: 0.25 gallons
Report Description
****WEB REPORT**** AT APPROXIMATELY 12:15 PM, TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 4, 2012, WHILE MAKING HIS ROUNDS, THE CHEOAH/SANTEETLAH SHIFT MECHANIC DISCOVERED THE SUMP PUMP FOR THE DOWNSTREAM SUMP AT SANTEETLAH POWER HOUSE RUNNING CONTINUALLY. UPON FURTHER INVESTIGATION, HE FOUND THE FLOAT WAS BROKEN OFF FROM THE CHAIN THAT WAS SUPPORTING THE FLOAT AND THE FLOAT WAS AT THE BOTTOM OF THE SUMP. HE IMMEDIATELY STOPPED THE PUMP AND SUMMONED ANOTHER MECHANIC TO HELP HIM RETRIEVE THE FLOAT AND REPAIR IT. ONCE OUTSIDE THE POWER HOUSE, THE EMPLOYEES NOTICED AN OIL SHEEN ON THE WATER. THE SHEEN WAS IN THE FORM OF A RAINBOW. IT IS ESTIMATED THAT APPROXIMATELY 1 QUART OR LESS OF OIL WAS DISCHARGED. THE OIL WAS IN THE IMMEDIATE VICINITY OF THE POWER HOUSE. THERE WAS A SLIGHT BREEZE OF APPROXIMATELY 5-8 MPH WHICH WAS BLOWING DOWNSTREAM. THE WIND WAS CAUSING THE SHEEN TO BE PUSHED ALONG THE BANK TOWARD THE BOAT DOCK AT RHYMERS FERRY. THE INITIAL SIZE OF THE SHEEN WAS APPROXIMATELY 20 FEET OUT FROM THE POWER HOUSE AND APPROXIMATELY 30 FT DOWNSTREAM. AS THE WIND CONTINUED TO BLOW AND MOVE THE SHEEN, THE SHEEN BECAME SMALLER IN DIAMETER AND LONGER DOWNSTREAM. THE ROCKS AT THE BOTTOM OF THE BANK (APPROXIMATELY 3 FT OF WATER DEPTH) COULD BE SEEN CLEARLY THROUGH THE RAINBOW IN THE WATER. CLEAN-UP WAS INITIATED IMMEDIATELY AND CONTINUED UNTIL WEATHER/FOG MOVED INTO THE LOCATION WHICH IMPACTED CLEAN-UP EFFORTS. THE CLEAN-UP OF THE OIL CONTINUED THIS MORNING, WEDNESDAY SEPT. 5, 2012 WITH THE SMALL AMOUNT OF OIL STILL TRAPPED WITH BOOMS ON THE WATER. CLEAN-UP EFFORTS ARE EXPECTED TO BE COMPLETED TODAY AND ALL OIL WILL BE REMOVED FROM THE WATER.

properties.content:
Report Details

SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 28.605810, -81.337642 (Approximated from CITY_STATE)
Report Description
*****WEB REPORT***** TWO YOUNG MEN WERE REGRADING SITE SOILS DUE TO DRAINAGE ISSUES THIS A.M. AND ENCOUNTERED A RESIN TYPE ODOR AND STARTED TO FEEL UN-WELL. THEY RESEARCHED THE SITE AND FOUND IT TO BE AN NPL SITE AND BECAME MORE WELL WORRIED ABOUT POTENTIAL EXPOSURES. ORANGE COUNTY FD AND HAZ-MAT RESPONDED TO THE SCENE. Report Description
***WEB REPORT*** AT APPROXIMATELY 0535 HOURS THIS MORNING PG&E DISPATCH RECEIVED A CALL REGARDING A STRUCTURE FIRE AT THE OLD JC PENNY BUILDING AT FULTON MALL IN FRESNO. ELECTRIC T-MAN DISPATCHED AT 0548 HOURS. GAS SERVICE REPRESENTATIVE ON SITE AT 0645 HOURS. CREWS ON SITE AT 0904 HOURS. A TRANSFORMER EXPLODED IN THE BASEMENT OF THE STRUCTURE AND AT THIS TIME IT IS NOT KNOWN IF THE EXPLOSION CAUSED THE LEAK OR IF THE GAS LEAK CAUSED THE EXPLOSION. THE SOURCE OF THE GAS LEAK IS A CURB VALVE ADJACENT TO THE STRUCTURE. GAS WAS SHUT OFF AT 1045 HOURS. FIRE DEPARTMENT, POLICE DEPARTMENT AND LOCAL MEDIA ON SCENE. ROADS ARE BARRICADED AND BUILDING EVACUATED. APPROXIMATELY 37 CUSTOMERS AFFECTED. NO INJURIES AND NO FATALITIES AS A RESULT OF THIS INCIDENT. DAMAGES ARE EXPECTED TO EXCEED $50,000.
